short: Multi-scale TCN (M06) and variable-length cropping (M03) are standard: head and augmentation are not separated, no run counts, robustness comes from the cropping; 85.3% LRW trails 93.2% today.
position: The paper [@martinez2020tcn] changes the temporal back end (M06), a multi-scale dilated TCN in place of a BGRU, and the training recipe (M03), a cosine schedule after a 50-word warm-up, with variable-length temporal cropping. Both are standard. Temporal convolution on LRW predates it and lost to Bi-LSTMs in three read priors [@stafylakis2017resnetlstm; @stafylakis2018pushing; @weng2019twostream]; only the multi-scale branching has no prior pattern hit. With both heads trained on variable-length clips the TCN leads 85.30% to 82.40% (Table 2), but no fixed-length TCN row, run count or dispersion is reported, and a [later] matched recipe with word boundaries and a four-layer 1024-unit BGRU gives 90.0% vs 89.7% [@ma2022trainingstrategies]. As the authors report (§5.3), frame-drop robustness comes from the cropping. LRW-1000 has no own BGRU baseline and the noise experiment names no corpus. Today 85.3% on LRW trails 93.2% without word boundaries [@ahn2024syncvsr].
